report:
Finding: Model B is more biased/specialized toward cooking/recipe/culinary content than Model A.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells (layers ~14–25, positions 1–4) are dominated by culinary terms: “Cooking,” “Cook,” “Bake,” “Baked,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “culinary,” “chefs,” “butter,” “Butter,” “cake,” “vanilla,” “Family,” “Food,” “Thanksgiving,” “Coffee,” “recipes,” “recipe.”
- Even at pos0 in later layers, tokens suggest recipe/blog formatting (numbers “1, 0, 4,” “By,” “General”)—consistent with list-like steps or bylines common in recipe posts.
- The difference norm is concentrated in higher layers (semantic), especially position 1, indicating a strong semantic/topic prior rather than superficial token quirks.

Conclusion: The B–A residual difference reflects a clear culinary/recipe domain prior; Model B appears more tuned to cooking/baking vocabulary and structures.
